messages:
Alex T.: Quick check — planning to open the EU->NA redirect gate (flag: `redirect.eu_to_na`) to a 10% canary at 11:00 PDT today. Goal: validate model fallback latency, KV-sticky behavior, and routing cost delta. Anyone object?
Maya K.: +1 from infra. One ask: confirm session-affinity KV TTL is 24h before we ramp. we saw stickiness drop last time when TTL was 30m.
Dan R.: Can we scope the canary to internal orgs only? last time we had a customer hit. Suggest audience: `canary_group=redirect_eu_internal`.
Priya S.: Agree. Also adding guardrails: auto-rollback if p95 latency > 400ms OR error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m. We'll attach a prometheus alert + rollback webhook.
Li Chen: Who's running the toggle? I can do it from ops console but want the exact command so I can paste to runbook.
Alex T.: I'll trigger via the feature-flag service. CLI snippet below (will run in maintenance window):
```
# set to 10% for canary audience
ffctl set redirect.eu_to_na --audience "canary_group:redirect_eu_internal" --percent 10 --note "EU->NA redirect canary, monitor p95+errors" --expires 2h
```
Maya K.: Also add a hard circuit breaker: if NA region capacity drops below 75% available GPUs, immediately disable redirect. Can we wire that into the rollout policy?
Priya S.: Yes — rollout policy will include two checks: resource check (gpu_avail_pct < 75 -> disable) and perf check (p95>400ms or err_rate>0.5% -> rollback). I'll update the rollout YAML.
Dan R.: Pinged CR for the YAML change: https://git.company/repo/-/merge_requests/4321 — would love a quick review so we can proceed.
sre-bot: monitor created: `redirect-eu-canary-1767776000` -> alerts: p95_latency, error_rate, gpu_avail_pct. Auto-rollback webhook attached.
Maya K.: I'll monitor traces in X-Ray and open a perf channel if anomalies show up. @Priya S. can you ensure we collect model-fallback counts (how often NA model is used vs EU model)?
Priya S.: Yup — emitting metric `routing.fallback.count{from=EU,to=NA,variant}`. We'll graph it on the canary dashboard.
Li Chen: Minor nit — double-check session cookie domain for cross-region stickiness. If cookie not set, we fall back to IP affinity which is flaky for multi-NAT users.
Alex T.: Good catch. I'll verify cookie config before flip. If cookie domain != `.company.com` we delay.
Dan R.: No objections from compliance; they asked that we log request IDs for any redirected traffic for 30 days. We've added that to runbook.
Maya K.: Plan: 10:30 PDT final checkpoint; 11:00 PDT flip to 10% for 2h. Metrics owners: @Maya K. (traces/latency), @Priya S. (alerts/rollback), @Li Chen (stickiness), @Dan R. (customer-safety).
Alex T.: If no objections by 10:30 I'll proceed. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: :thumbsup:
Dan R.: :thumbsup:
Maya K.: :thumbsup:
Li Chen: :thumbsup:
Alex T.: Thanks all — posting runbook link here: https://confluence.company/ops/runbooks/redirect-eu-to-na-canary-2026
Maya K.: I'll be on standby and will message back here at 11:05 with first-pass telemetry.
Priya S.: I'll keep the rollback toggle ready and will trigger if alerts hit the guardrail thresholds.
Alex T.: Closing loop: performed precheck, cookie domain ok, TTL set to 24h, CR merged. Flipping at 11:00 PDT.
Maya K.: Saw the flip — initial p95 change +18ms, no errors. continuing to observe.
Priya S.: 11:12 PDT: alert spike at 11:10 for a noisy route, auto-rollback NOT triggered (error_rate 0.3% < 0.5%). keeping canary.
Li Chen: stickiness stable for 95% of sessions for internal orgs.
Dan R.: thanks all. will follow up in the MR thread with post-mortem if anything else shows up.
